inputs.original_text: Tom Homan’s refusal to rule out immigration enforcement at polling places is alarming. Asking what Democrats are “afraid of” turns a serious threat into a taunt: visible enforcement could intimidate immigrant communities and discourage people from participating in elections. The Trump administration’s inconsistent answers only deepen the concern. People should be able to vote without fearing that an encounter with immigration authorities is waiting nearby.
inputs.modified_text: The refusal to rule out immigration enforcement at polling places is a threat in itself. When officials ask what Democrats are “afraid of,” they trivialize the fear that visible enforcement could keep immigrant communities from voting. That is how unequal power works: the people already most vulnerable to state intimidation are made to bear the cost of political games. The Trump administration’s inconsistent answers make clear that basic protections for voters cannot be left to official assurances. No one should have to choose between participating in democracy and fearing immigration authorities.
